title: BenchmarkSuite
description: Tournament-protocol benchmark suite manifest. The verifier is declared as a generic command, with TS-on-Bun the convention but multiple escape hatches supported (python3, wolframscript, octave, Rscript, julia, sage, gap). v2 (2026-05-23, bead wr2): optional golden.n_heads / golden.n_tiers for multi-head, multi-tier corpora (ADR-0028 bench-to-corpus migration; ADR-0040/0041 mega-anchor structure); optional verifier.checks[].machine_checkable and verifier.checks[].applies_when for queryable check metadata.

domain.description: Mathematical domain: linalg, cas, integration, ode, optimisation, ...

verifier.description: Declares how to run the verifier. The verifier reads {input, candidate, id} on stdin and emits {pass, reason, checks: {name: {pass, detail}}} on stdout, exiting 0. Language-neutral.

args.description: ${SUITE_ROOT} is substituted to the absolute path of the suite directory.

tolerance_source.description: Citation backing the tolerance choice — e.g. 'Higham 2002 §20.6'.

machine_checkable.description: True when the check is automatically verifiable by the declared verifier command; false when the check requires manual inspection or out-of-band judgement. Semantically defaults to true when omitted.
machine_checkable.$comment: Added in v2 (2026-05-23, bead scientist-workbench-corpus-wr2). Mirrors workbench's InvariantEntry.machine_checkable; lets the DuckDB verifier_checks table flag automatable vs manual checks for downstream analytics.

applies_when.description: Free-form predicate descriptor naming the condition under which the check is applicable — e.g. "status == 'infeasible'". When the predicate is false the check is skipped (N/A) rather than failed.
applies_when.$comment: Added in v2 (2026-05-23, bead scientist-workbench-corpus-wr2). Currently a string descriptor — interpreted by the verifier, not parsed by the runner — making conditionality queryable from DuckDB without committing to a formal predicate language yet.

n_heads.description: Number of independent oracle/output heads per input, for multi-head bench corpora (e.g. erf-anchor's 6 heads: erf, erfc, erfcx, erfi, w(z), Fresnel).
n_heads.$comment: Added in v2 (2026-05-23, bead scientist-workbench-corpus-wr2). Targets erf-anchor (B18) and besselj-anchor (B19) migrations per ADR-0028; structural metadata for ADR-0040/0041 mega-anchor corpora.

n_tiers.description: Number of tiers (per-precision, per-difficulty, or per-region strata) the golden inputs are partitioned into. Tier semantics are corpus-specific and documented in the suite's description.
n_tiers.$comment: Added in v2 (2026-05-23, bead scientist-workbench-corpus-wr2). Targets erf-anchor's 8 tiers and besselj-anchor's 10 tiers per ADR-0028 / ADR-0040 / ADR-0041; lets DuckDB queries group cases by tier without parsing free-form descriptions.

generate_cmd.description: Shell command (run from suite root) to regenerate inputs.json + expected.json. Escape-hatch friendly: most generators are SciPy/SymPy/Mathematica because of oracle availability.
